english.title: Endangering aircraft - Aviation Security Act 1982
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) unlawfully and intentionally on board an aircraft in flight committed an act of violence which was likely to endanger the safety of that aircraft

english.notes:
(i) Section 2(3) of the Aviation Security Act 1982 provides that the offence covers acts committed within the United Kingdom or elsewhere regardless of the nationality of the offender and the State in which the aircraft is registered.
(ii) Section 2(4) of the Act provides exceptions to the offence for acts committed in relation to aircrafts used in military, customs or police service outside the United Kingdom and not by United Kingdom nationals.
(iii) Section 2(6) of the Act provides the meaning of unlawfully.
(iv) Section 2(7) of the Act provides the meaning of act of violence.
(v) Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property.

other.powersofarrest:
Arrest without warrant
Section 7(1) of the Aviation Security Act 1982 provides a power of arrest without warrant where a person on an aircraft or about to embark an aircraft intends to commit this offence.
other.penalty:
INDICTMENT: Life imprisonment.
